findings.title: Derived website name bypasses TL0 privacy filtering
findings.body: `include_website_name` is not the serializer predicate `include_website_name?`, and `website_name` is not covered by `untrusted_attributes`. The serializer therefore includes this derived value even when `include_website?` hides a TL0 user's website from anonymous viewers. Because `website_name` contains the website host and may include its path, anonymous users can still see information the website restriction is meant to hide. Apply the same restriction to `website_name` and add a regression test for an anonymous viewer.

findings.title: Website labels drop non-default ports
findings.body: `URI#host` excludes the port. For a profile URL such as `https://example.org:8443/user`, `website_name` becomes `example.org` (or `example.org/user` when the host matches the instance), whereas the previous display included `:8443`. The profile label can therefore misidentify the endpoint, especially when multiple services share a host. Preserve an explicitly specified port in the displayed host.
